**Exposure:** In its fiscal 2021 10-K, Kroger said it is subject to commodity price risk from its purchases of meat, seafood and dairy products, among other food items. It purchases, manufactures and sells commodity-related food products, so price volatility creates risk, and the price and availability of these commodities directly affect its results of operations. It is also exposed to changes in diesel and unleaded fuel prices. Fuel contracts mostly use index-based pricing, and because indices may move at different paces, operating results could be affected positively or negatively in the short term if fuel prices change suddenly [1].

**Management steps:**
- It uses pricing features embedded in supply contracts, such as fixed-price and price-to-be-fixed contracts, and can raise or lower retail prices as commodity prices change [1].
- It has fixed price contracts to buy electricity and natural gas for part of its energy needs. It expects to take delivery in the normal course of business, so these contracts qualify as normal purchases [1].
- It had no commodity derivative contracts outstanding at January 29, 2022 or January 30, 2021 [1].
